questions.question: The Red Fort is located in:
questions.questionHtml: The Red Fort is located in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Delhi

Key Points

  • The Red Fort is situated in Delhi, the capital city of India.
  • It was constructed by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the mid-17th century.
  • The fort served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years, until 1857.
  • It is an iconic symbol of India's rich history and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
  • The Red Fort is named for its massive enclosing walls of red sandstone and is a prominent tourist attraction.

Additional Information

  • Delhi is a city rich in history and has many other significant landmarks such as the Qutub Minar, India Gate, and Humayun's Tomb.
  • Every year on Independence Day (15th August), the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag at the main gate of the Red Fort and delivers a nationally broadcast speech from its ramparts.
  • The architecture of the Red Fort reflects a blend of Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles.
  • Major structures within the fort include the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience), and the Rang Mahal (Palace of Colors).
  • The Red Fort's design and layout influenced later buildings and gardens in Delhi, Rajasthan, Punjab, Kashmir, and elsewhere.

questions.question: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is located in _____.
questions.questionHtml: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is located in _____.
questions.solution: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is located in Sasaram, Bihar. It was built in memory of Sher Shah Suri, who founded the Suri empire after defeating the Mughal empire. Designed by Mir Muhammad Aliwal Khan, the tomb is an example of Indo-Islamic Architecture. It is also known as the Second Taj Mahal of India and is built in between an artificial lake.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal was built by:
questions.questionHtml: The Taj Mahal was built by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan

Key Points

  • Shah Jahan commissioned the construction of the Taj Mahal in 1632.
  • The Taj Mahal was built as a mausoleum for his beloved wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
  • It is located in Agra, India, and is one of the most famous and recognizable buildings in the world.
  • The construction of the Taj Mahal was completed in 1653.
  • It is an outstanding example of Mughal architecture, which combines elements from Islamic, Persian, Ottoman Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.

Additional Information

  • The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and attracts millions of visitors every year.
  • It is often referred to as the "Crown of Palaces" and is considered one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
  • The white marble structure is adorned with intricate carvings and inlaid with precious stones.
  • The Taj Mahal complex includes a main gateway, a garden, a mosque, a guest house, and several other palatial buildings.
  • The monument stands as a symbol of enduring love and architectural brilliance.

questions.question: The ‘flag-raising’ ceremony by the Prime Minister of India on Independence Day is held at which of the following places in Delhi?
questions.questionHtml: The ‘flag-raising’ ceremony by the Prime Minister of India on Independence Day is held at which of the following places in Delhi?
questions.solution: The flag-raising ceremony on Independence Day in India is held at the Red Fort in Delhi. The Prime Minister unfurls the flag every year, with some having the opportunity to do so multiple times. Narendra Modi has been hoisting the flag since 2014, while Atal Bihari Vajpayee is the only non-Congress Prime Minister to have unfurled the flag at Red Fort six times.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Statue of Unity situated?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following states is the Statue of Unity situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1

Key Points

  • The Statue of Unity is located in the state of Gujarat.
  • It is a colossal statue of Indian statesman and independence activist Vallabhbhai Patel, who was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.
  • The statue is situated on the Narmada River in the Kevadiya colony, facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam.
  • Standing at a height of 182 meters (597 feet), it is currently the tallest statue in the world.
  • The Statue of Unity was inaugurated on 31st October 2018, marking the 143rd birth anniversary of Sardar Patel.

Additional Information

  • The statue was designed by Indian sculptor Ram V. Sutar.
  • It was built by Larsen & Toubro, an Indian multinational conglomerate, at a cost of approximately ₹2,989 crore (about USD 422 million).
  • The project aimed to inspire generations by highlighting Sardar Patel's role in unifying the country.
  • The site includes a museum, an exhibition hall, and a viewing gallery that offers a panoramic view of the surrounding region.
  • The Statue of Unity has become a major tourist attraction, drawing visitors from all over the world.

questions.question: ​The ruins of the ancient city of Hampi - capital of Vijayanagara - is located in which present day Indian state?
questions.questionHtml: ​The ruins of the ancient city of Hampi - capital of Vijayanagara - is located in which present day Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Karnataka

Key Points

  • ​The ruins of the ancient city of Hampi is a historical site located in Karnataka.
  • It is a UNESCO world heritage site and was granted that status in the year 1986.
  • It was established as Vidyanagar by Harihara and Buka, the founders of the Sangama dynasty, in the memory of their guru Vidyaranya.
  • Ancient temples, ruins of forts, and aquatic structures are the major attractions.
  • Temples related to Hinduism as well as Buddhism are found here.
  • Virupaksha temple, Hemakuta Hill temple, Vijay Vittal temple are the major Hindu temples.

Vijayanagar Empire (1336 - 1580):

  • This empire flourished on the banks of River Tungabhadra.
  • The Sangam, the Suluvas, the Tuluvas, and the Arivadu were the ruling dynasties of this empire.

Additional Information

  • The last ruler Virupaksha - II was assassinated by his commander-in-chief Saluva Narasimha.

questions.question: Siachen in Himalayas is:
questions.questionHtml: Siachen in Himalayas is:
questions.solution: Siachen is a glacier located in the eastern Karakoram range in the Himalayas. The Siachen Glacier is one of the largest glaciers outside the polar regions and is strategically significant, often referred to as the highest battlefield on Earth due to the military presence of neighboring countries. National parks are protected areas for conservation purposes, dams are built for water storage and hydroelectric power generation, and lakes are large bodies of water surrounded by land.

questions.question: Where is the Mahabodhi temple situated?
questions.questionHtml: Where is the Mahabodhi temple situated?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Bodh Gaya.

Key Points 

  • The Mahabodhi Temple Complex, Bodh Gaya lies 115 km south of the state capital of Bihar, Patna and 16 km from the district headquarters at Gaya, in Eastern India.
  • It is one of the four holy sites related to the life of the Lord Buddha, and particularly to the attainment of Enlightenment.
  • The property encompasses the greatest remains of the 5th-6th century A.D in the Indian sub-continent belonging to this period of antiquity.
  • The property has a total area of 4.8600 ha.
  • The Mahabodhi Temple Complex is the first temple built by Emperor Asoka in the 3rd century B.C., and the present temple dates from the 5th–6th centuries.
  • It is one of the earliest Buddhist temples built entirely in brick, still standing, from the late Gupta period and it is considered to have had significant influence in the development of brick architecture over the centuries.

questions.question: Somnath temple is situated on coast of which state?
questions.questionHtml: Somnath temple is situated on coast of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

Key Points

  • Somnath is an ancient temple town in the state of Gujarat 
  • It is located in Prabhas Patan in Saurashtra, Gujarat. 
  • It is among the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva in India, it is the first one.
  • The Somnath shrine is considered as an eternal shrine; it was destroyed several times; however, it was rebuilt again and again. 
  • Lastly, it was rebuilt in 1947 after Vallabhbhai Patel.
Additional Information

Triveni Sangam

  • It means 'the holy confluence of three rivers' - Kapila, Hiran and Saraswati.
  • It is believed that the Pandavas had visited the place to take a holy bath and built five temples of Lord Shiva here too.
  • Temples like Lakshminarayan temple and Gita Mandir are located on the banks of the ghat.

Shree Parshuram Temple

  • It is a temple dedicated to Lord Parshuram and located on the banks of Triveni. There are two ancient kunds in the premises of the temple.

Gita Mandir

  • This temple is also located on the banks of the Triveni Sangam Ghat.
  • There are 18 marble pillars in the temple on which the divine shlokas from Shrimad Bhagavad Geeta are engraved in Sanskrit.

Bhalka Teerth

  • The temple is considered a place where Lord Krishna was hit by an arrow that was shot by a hunter, Jara. 

Shree Shashibhushan Mahadev and Bhidbhanjan Ganapatiji Temple:

  • Lord Shashibhushan (the Moon God) along with Bhidbhanjan (savior form of Lord Ganesha) is worshipped here. ​

Important Points

  • CM of Gujarat: Bhupendra Patel 
  • Governor of Gujarat: Acharya Devvart

questions.question: The Char-Dham Highway Project will connect four holy places: Yamnotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath. To which Indian state do these places belong?

questions.question: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
questions.questionHtml: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sasaram.

  • Sher Shah Suri was a Pathan from Bihar who founded the Suri empire after defeating the Mughal empire.
  • In his memory, a tomb designed by Mir Muhammad Aliwal Khan was built in Sasaram, Bihar and it is an example of Indo-Islamic Architecture.

Important Points

  • Sher Shah Suri died in a gunpowder explosion in the fort of Kalinjar.
  • The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is also known as the Second Taj Mahal of India as it is built in between an artificial lake.

​Mistake Points

  • In Delhi, the construction of Purana Qila was begun during the time of Humayun which was continued till the time of Sher Shah Suri.
  • The son of Suri, Salim Shah Suri built the Salimgarh fort in Delhi.
  • Grand Trunk Road connecting Central Asia and India was built by Sher Shah Suri.

     Sher Shah Suri tomb in Sasaram, Bihar

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states were the remains of the ancient Vikramshila University discovered?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following Indian states were the remains of the ancient Vikramshila University discovered?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bihar.

Key Points

  • Vikramshila is an ancient site located 40 km away from the Bhagalpur city of Bihar.
  • The small town is famous for housing Vikramshila University, which was built under the guidance of Dharmapala, a Pala King of the 8th century AD.
  • Situated on top of the hills along the banks of the river Ganges, the university became a learning centre of Tantric Buddhism.
  • Over the years, Vikramshila became one of the most popular Buddhist destinations in India and a major tourist spot in Bihar. 
  • It prospered for about four centuries before it was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji along with the other major centres of Buddhism in India around 1193.

Important Points

  • During the Pala Empire, Vikramashila, along with Nalanda and Odantapuri, was one of India's three most prominent Buddhist monasteries.
  • In response to a perceived decrease in the quality of study at Nalanda, the Pala ruler Dharmapala (783–820 AD) founded Vikramashila.

questions.question: Which of the following is located in Gujarat?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is located in Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rani-ki-Vav.

Key Points

  • Rani ki Vav:
    • It is a very famous stepwell in Gujarat. It is situated in the town of Patan, Gujarat.
    • It is located on the bank of the Saraswati river. It was rediscovered and restored in the 1980s by the Archaeological Survey of India.
    • It is one of the UNESCO's World Heritage Sites since 2014.
    • Its architecture is very defining as it was made in the form of an inverted temple.
    • It is divided into seven levels of stairs, which have sculptural panels.
    • It was constructed during the rule of the Chalukyas dynasty.​

Additional Information

  • Alai Darwaza:
    • The Alai Darwaza is the main gate from the southern side of the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque in the Qutub Minar complex.
    • Allaudin Khilji constructed Alai Darwaza, the Palace of a thousand pillars, and the Fort of Siri.
  • Humayun Tomb:
    • Humayun's tomb is located in Delhi. It was built in the 1560s, with the patronage of Humayun's son, the great Emperor Akbar.
    • it was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent. It inspired several major architectural innovations, culminating in the construction of the Taj Mahal.
    • Humayun's Tomb, Delhi is the earliest example of the double dome in Mughal Architecture.
    • The double or double-layered dome has its outer layer which supports the white marble exterior, while the inner part gives shape to the cavernous interior volume.
    • It was designed by the architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyath. It includes other contemporary, 16th-century Mughal garden-tombs such as Nila Gumbad, Isa Khan, Bu Halima, Afsarwala, Barber's Tomb, and the complex where the craftsmen employed for the Building of Humayun's Tomb stayed, the Arab Serai.
  • Humayun's garden-tomb is also called the dormitory of the Mughals as in the cells are buried over 150 Mughal family members.
  • Bibi ka Maqbara:
    • Bibi ka Maqbara' is a tomb situated in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, India.
    • The Bibi-Ka-Maqbara is a beautiful mausoleum of Rabia-ul-Daurani alias Dilras Banu Begum, the wife of the Mughal Emperor Aurangazeb (1658-1707 A.D.).
    • This mausoleum is believed to be constructed by Prince Azam Shah in memory of his mother from 1651 to 1661 A.D. An inscription found on the main entrance door mentions.
    • Source: (Archeological Survey of India, Ministry of Culture).

questions.question: The famous Hirakud Captive Thermal Power plant is located in which of the following states?
questions.questionHtml: The famous Hirakud Captive Thermal Power plant is located in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Odisha.

Key Points

  • Hirakud Captive Thermal Power plant is located in the town of Burla in Sambalpur district of Odisha.
  • The plant is owned by Hindalco Industries, a subsidiary of Aditya Birla Group.
  • The plant has a capacity of generating 467.5 MW of electricity.
  • The power plant is located near the Hirakud Dam, which is the longest earthen dam in the world and is situated on the Mahanadi river.
Additional Information

  • Andhra Pradesh - Andhra Pradesh has several thermal power plants, including Simhadri Super Thermal Power Plant, Rayalaseema Thermal Power Plant, and Vijayawada Thermal Power Plant, but Hirakud Captive Thermal Power plant is not located in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: In which Indian state the archaeological site of the Paleolithic period, the "Bhimbetka Rock Shelters" is situated?
questions.questionHtml: In which Indian state the archaeological site of the Paleolithic period, the "Bhimbetka Rock Shelters" is situated?
questions.solution:

  • The name of the archaeological site is related to the Hindu deity ‘Bheem’ and roughly translates to the sitting place of Bheem.

questions.question: The ancient city of Dholavira, is located in which state?
questions.questionHtml: The ancient city of Dholavira, is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gujarat.
Key Points
  • The ancient city of Dholavira is located in the state of Gujarat.
  • Dholavira is one of the largest and most prominent archaeological sites in India, belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization.
  • The city was discovered in 1967-68 by archaeologist Jagat Pati Joshi, and since then, several excavations have been conducted to uncover its rich history.
  • The Tropic of Cancer is where Dholavira is located.
  • It is the most well-known Indus Valley Civilization archeological site in India and one of the five biggest Harappan sites.
  • It is situated on Khadir Bet Island in the Great Rann of Kutch's Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary.

Additional Information

  • Madhya Pradesh is a state in central India known for its rich cultural heritage and diverse wildlife. It does not have any significant ancient city belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization.
  • Rajasthan is a state in northwestern India known for its historical forts, palaces, and temples. It has several ancient sites belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization, such as Kalibangan and Ganeriwala, but not Dholavira.
  • Karnataka is a state in southern India known for its rich history, art, and literature. It does not have any significant ancient city belonging to the Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.question: Which of the following is the world's largest delta?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the world's largest delta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta​.


Key Points

  • Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is the largest delta in the world.
  • The deposition of sediment that is carried by a river created a landform called a river delta.
  • The Ganges Delta also called Sunderban Delta is situated in the Bengal region of the Indian subcontinent and also in Bangladesh.
  • The delta surface area of some 100.000 km2. 
  • The Ganges Delta is formed by three major rivers the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Megna river. 
  • Ganges Delta is also one of the most fertile regions in the world.

Additional Information

Delta

Feature

Arcuate

It is a fan-shaped delta where the deposition is maximum at the centre.

These deltas are composed of coarse sediments.

example-Ganga, Indus, Nile, Volga, Rhine etc.

Bird’s Foot

The irregular shape of the delta forms that extends out into the water well beyond the shoreline.

The action of the river is stronger than the action of waves.

The deposition is along the distributaries.

Example-Mississippi

Cuspate

It is tooth-shaped.

It forms where the river drops sediment onto a straight shoreline.

Example-Ebro delta in Spain and Tiber delta in Italy

Estuarine

It forms when a river empties into a long, narrow estuary that is eventually filled with sediments.

Those mouths of rivers are called estuaries.

These estuaries submerged into marine waters and ocean currents remove the sediments brought by rivers.

Example- Narmada and Tapi delta

questions.question: Which of the following cities is called the Silicon Valley of India due to its prominence in the IT industry?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following cities is called the Silicon Valley of India due to its prominence in the IT industry?
questions.solution: Bengaluru, known as the Silicon Valley of India, is a prominent IT hub with numerous tech companies, startups, and research institutions. It hosts headquarters of major Indian tech firms like Infosys and Wipro, and Indian offices of global giants like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. The city fosters a vibrant startup culture and is also recognized for its pleasant climate, earning the nickname "Garden City of India." Major educational institutions like IISc and IIMB are located there. Bengaluru's IT growth began in the late 1980s and 1990s, supported by favorable government policies and technology parks. Its infrastructure and cosmopolitan culture attract professionals globally.

questions.question: The idols of which three Gods are installed in Jagannath Temple, Puri?
questions.questionHtml: The idols of which three Gods are installed in Jagannath Temple, Puri?
questions.solution: The Jagannath Temple in Puri is dedicated to Lord Jagannath, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. It also houses the idols of Balabhadra (Jagannath's elder brother) and Subhadra (their sister). The temple is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites. The idol of Jagannath is made of wood and is replaced every twelve or nineteen years through a ritual called Nabakalebara. The temple is renowned for its annual Ratha Yatra festival. Non-Hindus cannot enter the temple but can view it from the nearby Raghunandan Library.

questions.questionHtml: Who among the following built the Hawa Mahal in Jaipur?
questions.solution: The Hawa Mahal in Jaipur was built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh in 1799. The Hawa Mahal, also known as the "Palace of Winds," is a five-story palace in Jaipur that was built for the women of the royal household to observe street festivals and processions without being seen by the public.

questions.question: The famous ‘Pashupatinath Temple’ is located in which country from the following?
questions.questionHtml: The famous ‘Pashupatinath Temple’ is located in which country from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nepal.

Key Points

  • The famous 'Pashupatinath Temple' is located in Nepal.
  • Pashupatinath Temple is a sacred Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and is situated on the banks of the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Nepal.
  • It is one of the most significant Hindu temples of Lord Shiva in the world and is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
  • The temple attracts thousands of pilgrims and tourists from all over the world every year, especially during the Maha Shivaratri festival.

Additional Information

  • Nepal is a landlocked country in South Asia, located mainly in the Himalayas, and is known for its rich cultural heritage and natural beauty.
  • Besides Pashupatinath Temple, Nepal is also home to other famous heritage sites such as Lumbini (the birthplace of Lord Buddha) and the ancient city of Bhaktapur.
  • The official language of Nepal is Nepali, and the currency used is the Nepalese Rupee (NPR).
  • Nepal shares its borders with China to the north and India to the south, east, and west.

questions.question: Jama Masjid in Delhi was built by ______.

questions.solution: Shah Jahan was the Mughal emperor from 1628 to 1658 and commissioned the construction of Jama Masjid in Delhi in 1650. Jama Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India and can accommodate up to 25,000 worshippers at a time.

questions.question: In which city is the Rajghat memorial situated?
questions.questionHtml: In which city is the Rajghat memorial situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Delhi

Key Points

  • Rajghat is a memorial dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi in Delhi, India.
  • It is located on the banks of the Yamuna river.
  • The memorial is a simple square platform made of black marble, marking the spot where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated on January 31, 1948.
  • Rajghat is a significant site for visitors, including various dignitaries from around the world, who pay their respects to the Father of the Nation.
  • The site is surrounded by a beautiful park with labeled trees planted by various dignitaries and heads of state.

Additional Information

  • Mahatma Gandhi was an influential leader of the Indian independence movement against British rule.
  • He is known for his philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and his role in leading India to independence through peaceful civil disobedience.
  • The Rajghat memorial is a place of national importance and is visited by millions of people every year.
  • Special ceremonies are held at Rajghat on Gandhi Jayanti (October 2) and other significant days.
  • The site also features an Eternal Flame that burns continuously in honor of Mahatma Gandhi's memory.

questions.question: Near which of the following cities are the Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka located?
questions.questionHtml: Near which of the following cities are the Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka located?
questions.solution: Bhimbetka's Rock Shelters, a UNESCO site in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh are believed to be one of India's oldest human habitation sites, dating back 10,000 years. With over 750 rock shelters and 400 caves, only 20 are open to the public.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Mughal architecture under Aurangzeb?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is an example of Mughal architecture under Aurangzeb?
questions.solution: The correct example of Mughal architecture under Aurangzeb is Moti Masjid, Delhi. It is a white marble mosque located inside the Red Fort complex. Aurangzeb built it between 1659 and 1660, and it cost Rs.160,000 to construct. The prayer hall has two aisles and three arches, with three bulbous domes on top. Taj Mahal was commissioned by Shah Jahan, Jama Masjid by Shah Jahan, and Qutab Minar by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
